findings.summary: Adaptive-experiment inference requires guarantees that explicitly account for adaptivity; recording exposures alone does not supply those guarantees.
findings.source: Bibaut & Kallus 2025, Annual Review of Statistics and Its Application, DOI 10.1146/annurev-statistics-040522-015431

findings.summary: Data splitting permits an otherwise unconstrained selection procedure if selection remains independent of the inference split; it is a robust validity floor though not generally power-optimal.

Selective inference, randomized selection, and safe/e-value testing offer validity under particular adaptive processes, but their guarantees are process-specific and do not automatically cover opaque outcome-responsive hypothesis generation.
sources: Fithian, Sun & Taylor, Optimal Inference After Model Selection
Grunwald, de Heide & Koolen 2024, JRSS B, DOI 10.1093/jrsssb/qkae011

findings.summary: Evidence-state visibility can change experimenter behavior and protocol independently of statistical optional-stopping validity; protected feedback visibility should therefore be prospectively masked or bounded during candidate generation.
findings.source: Sadibolova & Terhune 2025, Behavior Research Methods, DOI 10.3758/s13428-025-02813-0
